title: Pizza Order Builder with Overloaded Constructors
description:
Bro Code's Java Course teaches that overloaded constructors allow a class to have multiple ways of being instantiated depending on how many arguments are provided.

In this challenge, design a Pizza class that features overloaded constructors to handle various custom orders:
- Pizza(String bread)
- Pizza(String bread, String sauce)
- Pizza(String bread, String sauce, String cheese)
- Pizza(String bread, String sauce, String cheese, String topping)

The program reads an integer N (1 to 4) representing the number of ingredients specified by the customer, followed by the ingredient names. Instantiate the Pizza using the appropriate constructor and print the complete ingredient list.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N (1 <= N <= 4) representing the number of ingredients provided.
The second line contains N space-separated strings representing the ingredients in order: bread, sauce, cheese, topping.
outputFormat:
Print the pizza specification in the format:
"Bread: <bread> | Sauce: <sauce> | Cheese: <cheese> | Topping: <topping>"
If an ingredient was not provided in the constructor, display "None" for that field.
constraints: Ingredient names contain only letters with no spaces
sampleOutput: Bread: ThickCrust | Sauce: Tomato | Cheese: Mozzarella | Topping: Pepperoni

testCases.expectedOutput: Bread: ThickCrust | Sauce: Tomato | Cheese: Mozzarella | Topping: Pepperoni
Bread: ThinCrust | Sauce: Barbecue | Cheese: None | Topping: None
Bread: FlatBread | Sauce: None | Cheese: None | Topping: None
Bread: StuffedCrust | Sauce: Pesto | Cheese: Cheddar | Topping: None

sourceScreenshot: Bro Code Java Full Course (03:16:39 - Overloaded Constructors)
explanation: Overloaded constructors demonstrate constructor delegation and handling variable initialization configurations cleanly.

title: Car Dealership Inventory with Object Arrays
description:
In Java, an array can store objects just like primitive data types. Storing objects in an array allows developers to manage collections of complex entities efficiently.

Create a Car class with attributes: make (String), model (String), and year (int). Read N cars into an array of Car objects (`Car[] garage`), then iterate through the array to display each car's information and identify the newest car in the dealership.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of cars.
The next N lines each contain make, model, and year separated by spaces.
outputFormat:
Print each car on a separate line in the format: "<year> <make> <model>".
On the final line, print: "Newest Car: <year> <make> <model>".
constraints: Make and model are single words
sampleInput:
3
Tesla Model3 2023
Ford Mustang 2021
Toyota Camry 2024
sampleOutput:
2023 Tesla Model3
2021 Ford Mustang
2024 Toyota Camry
Newest Car: 2024 Toyota Camry

testCases.input:
3
Tesla Model3 2023
Ford Mustang 2021
Toyota Camry 2024
testCases.expectedOutput:
2023 Tesla Model3
2021 Ford Mustang
2024 Toyota Camry
Newest Car: 2024 Toyota Camry

2022 BMW M3
2022 Audi RS6
Newest Car: 2022 BMW M3

2019 Honda Civic
Newest Car: 2019 Honda Civic

sourceScreenshot: Bro Code Java Full Course (03:30:08 - Array of Objects)
explanation: Demonstrates instantiating an array of custom class instances and iterating over them.

title: Garage Parking Manager with Object Passing
description:
Object passing is the practice of passing an object of one class as an argument to a method of another class.

Create a Vehicle class with a name (String) attribute, and a Garage class with a fixed capacity C.
The Garage has a method `boolean park(Vehicle vehicle)`:
- If current parked vehicles < capacity C, the vehicle is accepted and the method prints: "Parked: <name> in Bay <bayIndex>" (1-based indexing).
- If the garage is full, it prints: "Garage Full: Cannot park <name>".
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer C representing garage capacity.
The second line contains an integer N representing the number of arriving vehicles.
The third line contains N space-separated vehicle names.
outputFormat:
Print the parking status for each arriving vehicle in order.
On the final line, print: "Total Parked: <count>/<capacity>".
sampleOutput:
Parked: BMW in Bay 1
Parked: Ferrari in Bay 2
Garage Full: Cannot park Tesla
Total Parked: 2/2

testCases.expectedOutput:
Parked: BMW in Bay 1
Parked: Ferrari in Bay 2
Garage Full: Cannot park Tesla
Total Parked: 2/2

Parked: Toyota in Bay 1
Parked: Honda in Bay 2
Total Parked: 2/3

Parked: Porsche in Bay 1
Garage Full: Cannot park Corvette
Total Parked: 1/1

sourceScreenshot: Bro Code Java Full Course (03:35:48 - Object Passing)
explanation: Illustrates inter-object communication where one class manages and interacts with instances of another.

title: Bank Account with Variable Scope & Static Interest Rate
description:
Bro Code emphasizes the distinction between local variables, instance variables, and static variables. A static variable belongs to the class itself, and all instances share that single copy.

Create a BankAccount class where:
- `annualInterestRate` is a `static double` shared across all accounts.
- `accountHolder` (String) and `balance` (double) are instance variables.
- A static method `setInterestRate(double rate)` modifies the shared rate.
- An instance method `applyAnnualInterest()` adds `(balance * annualInterestRate / 100.0)` to the account balance.

Given an initial interest rate, N accounts, and an updated interest rate, apply the updated rate to all accounts and print the updated balances.
inputFormat:
The first line contains double rate representing the new static interest rate percentage.
The second line contains an integer N representing the number of accounts.
The next N lines contain accountHolder (string) and balance (double).
outputFormat:
Print each account's updated balance in the format: "<holder>: <roundedBalance>".
Round balance to 2 decimal places.

testCases.expectedOutput: Charlie: 550.00

sourceScreenshot: Bro Code Java Full Course (03:40:27 - Static Keyword)
explanation: Illustrates how static class members apply globally across all created instances.

title: Hero RPG Character Custom toString Representation
description:
In Java, every class inherits from the Object class. Overriding the `toString()` method allows objects to return a descriptive textual representation rather than their memory hashcode.

Implement a Hero class with attributes: name (String), heroClass (String), level (int), and hp (int).
Override `toString()` to return:
"[Hero: <name> | Class: <heroClass> | Level: <level> | HP: <hp>]"

Read N heroes and print them directly using `System.out.println(hero)`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of heroes.
The next N lines each contain name, heroClass, level, and hp separated by spaces.
outputFormat: Print the custom string representation for each hero on a separate line.

[Hero: Arthur | Class: Warrior | Level: 15 | HP: 350]
[Hero: Merlin | Class: Mage | Level: 20 | HP: 210]

title: Vehicle Fleet Hierarchy with super Constructor Chaining
description:
Inheritance allows one class to acquire the attributes and methods of another. The `super` keyword refers to the superclass (parent) object, commonly used in constructor chaining to pass arguments to the parent constructor.

Design a class hierarchy:
- Base class `Vehicle` with attributes: brand (String) and topSpeed (int). Constructor: `Vehicle(String brand, int topSpeed)`.
- Derived class `Car` adds doors (int). Constructor uses `super(brand, topSpeed)`.
- Derived class `Bicycle` adds hasBell (boolean). Constructor uses `super(brand, topSpeed)`.

Read N vehicle entries and output their complete specifications.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of vehicles.
The next N lines each start with vehicle type ('CAR' or 'BIKE') followed by:
- For CAR: brand topSpeed doors
- For BIKE: brand topSpeed hasBell
outputFormat:
Print each vehicle:
- For CAR: "Car -> Brand: <brand>, Speed: <topSpeed> km/h, Doors: <doors>"
- For BIKE: "Bike -> Brand: <brand>, Speed: <topSpeed> km/h, Bell: <hasBell>"
sampleOutput:
Car -> Brand: Ferrari, Speed: 340 km/h, Doors: 2
Bike -> Brand: Trek, Speed: 45 km/h, Bell: true

testCases.expectedOutput:
Car -> Brand: Ferrari, Speed: 340 km/h, Doors: 2
Bike -> Brand: Trek, Speed: 45 km/h, Bell: true
Car -> Brand: Honda, Speed: 200 km/h, Doors: 4

testCases.input:
3
BIKE Giant 35 false
CAR Porsche 310 2
BIKE Scott 40 true
testCases.expectedOutput:
Bike -> Brand: Giant, Speed: 35 km/h, Bell: false
Car -> Brand: Porsche, Speed: 310 km/h, Doors: 2
Bike -> Brand: Scott, Speed: 40 km/h, Bell: true

sourceScreenshot: Bro Code Java Full Course (03:57:33 - Super Keyword)
explanation: Constructor chaining with super ensures base attributes are initialized before child extensions.

title: Animal Kingdom Sound Dispatcher with Method Overriding
description:
Method overriding allows a subclass to provide a specific implementation of a method that is already defined in its superclass.

Create a base class `Animal` with method `speak()` that prints "The animal makes a sound".
Create subclasses:
- `Dog`: overrides `speak()` to print "Dog goes *woof*"
- `Cat`: overrides `speak()` to print "Cat goes *meow*"
- `Cow`: overrides `speak()` to print "Cow goes *moo*"

Read N animal type strings and invoke `speak()` dynamically on each.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of animals.
The second line contains N space-separated animal names ('dog', 'cat', or 'cow').
outputFormat: Print the sound produced by each animal on a new line.
sampleOutput:
Dog goes *woof*
Cat goes *meow*
Cow goes *moo*

Dog goes *woof*
Cat goes *meow*
Cow goes *moo*

Cat goes *meow*
Dog goes *woof*

Cow goes *moo*

Dog goes *woof*
Cat goes *meow*

sourceScreenshot: Bro Code Java Full Course (03:53:45 - Method Overriding)
explanation: Subclasses provide specialized behaviors while adhering to the common base class contract.

title: Abstract Payment Gateway System
description:
Abstract classes cannot be instantiated and are used to define a blueprint for subclasses. An abstract method has a signature but no body; subclasses must implement all abstract methods.

Create an `abstract class Payment`:
- Protected attribute: `double amount`
- Constructor `Payment(double amount)`
- Abstract method: `abstract void processPayment()`

Implement concrete subclasses:
- `CreditCardPayment`: deducts 2% transaction fee and prints:
  "Paid $<amount> via Credit Card (Fee: $<fee> | Net: $<net>)"
- `PayPalPayment`: deducts 1.5% fee and prints:
  "Paid $<amount> via PayPal (Fee: $<fee> | Net: $<net>)"
- `CryptoPayment`: 0% fee (0.00 fee) and prints:
  "Paid $<amount> via Crypto (Fee: $0.00 | Net: $<amount>)"

Format currency to 2 decimal places.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of transactions.
The next N lines each contain the payment method ('CREDIT', 'PAYPAL', or 'CRYPTO') and amount (double).
outputFormat: Print the payment receipt for each transaction on a new line.
sampleOutput:
Paid $100.00 via Credit Card (Fee: $2.00 | Net: $98.00)
Paid $200.00 via PayPal (Fee: $3.00 | Net: $197.00)
Paid $50.00 via Crypto (Fee: $0.00 | Net: $50.00)

testCases.expectedOutput:
Paid $100.00 via Credit Card (Fee: $2.00 | Net: $98.00)
Paid $200.00 via PayPal (Fee: $3.00 | Net: $197.00)
Paid $50.00 via Crypto (Fee: $0.00 | Net: $50.00)
Paid $500.00 via PayPal (Fee: $7.50 | Net: $492.50)

Paid $1000.00 via Crypto (Fee: $0.00 | Net: $1000.00)
Paid $250.00 via Credit Card (Fee: $5.00 | Net: $245.00)

title: Secure User Profile with Strict Encapsulation
description:
Encapsulation hides an object's internal state and requires all interaction to occur through public getter and setter methods. This allows developers to validate data before updating attributes.

Create a UserAccount class with private fields: username, password, email.
Provide getters and setters with validation rules:
- `setPassword(String p)`: must be >= 8 chars and contain >= 1 digit.
- `setEmail(String e)`: must contain '@' and '.' after '@'.

Read registration attempts and output whether each profile was successfully created or rejected.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing registration attempts.
The next N lines each contain username, password, and email.
outputFormat:
For each user:
- If password fails: "Error: Weak password for <username>"
- If email fails: "Error: Invalid email for <username>"
- If both pass: "User <username> registered successfully"
constraints: Inputs are single words with no spaces
sampleInput:
3
Alice password123 alice@domain.com
Bob short bob@test.com
Charlie pass1234 charlie_at_test.com
sampleOutput:
User Alice registered successfully
Error: Weak password for Bob
Error: Invalid email for Charlie

testCases.input:
3
Alice password123 alice@domain.com
Bob short bob@test.com
Charlie pass1234 charlie_at_test.com
testCases.expectedOutput:
User Alice registered successfully
Error: Weak password for Bob
Error: Invalid email for Charlie
User Dave registered successfully

Error: Invalid email for Eve
User Frank registered successfully

explanation: Validating input parameters within encapsulation setters protects internal object consistency.

title: Smart Home Device Duplicator using Copy Constructors
description:
In Java, assigning one object variable to another (`b = a`) only copies the reference. To create a true independent clone, developers implement copy constructors.

Create a SmartDevice class with name, room, and brightness (0-100).
Provide a copy constructor `SmartDevice(SmartDevice other)`.
Read an original device configuration, clone it using the copy constructor, apply an updated brightness value ONLY to the copy, and print both objects to prove they maintain separate states.
inputFormat:
The first line contains name, room, and initial brightness of the original device.
The second line contains the updated brightness value for the copied device.
outputFormat:
Print:
"Original: <name> in <room> (Brightness: <originalBrightness>%)"
"Copy: <name> in <room> (Brightness: <updatedBrightness>%)"
constraints: Device and room names have no spaces
sampleOutput:
Original: LivingRoomLight in LivingRoom (Brightness: 75%)
Copy: LivingRoomLight in LivingRoom (Brightness: 30%)

testCases.expectedOutput:
Original: LivingRoomLight in LivingRoom (Brightness: 75%)
Copy: LivingRoomLight in LivingRoom (Brightness: 30%)

Original: KitchenLamp in Kitchen (Brightness: 100%)
Copy: KitchenLamp in Kitchen (Brightness: 50%)

Original: DeskFan in Office (Brightness: 40%)
Copy: DeskFan in Office (Brightness: 90%)

sourceScreenshot: Bro Code Java Full Course (04:27:30 - Copy Objects)
explanation: Copy constructors produce deep independent duplicates, preventing accidental shared state side-effects.

title: Shape Area & Perimeter Calculator via Abstract Classes
description:
Polymorphism allows objects of different classes to be treated as objects of a common superclass.

Create an abstract class `Shape` with abstract methods:
- `abstract double area()`
- `abstract double perimeter()`

Implement subclasses:
- `Circle`: radius r. Area = pi * r^2, Perimeter = 2 * pi * r (use Math.PI).
- `Rectangle`: width w, height h. Area = w * h, Perimeter = 2 * (w + h).

Read N shape commands and print each shape's computed area and perimeter formatted to 2 decimal places.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of shapes.
The next N lines each contain:
- 'CIRCLE <radius>'
- 'RECTANGLE <width> <height>'
outputFormat:
Print each shape formatted as:
"<Type> -> Area: <area>, Perimeter: <perimeter>" (formatted to 2 decimal places).
sampleOutput:
Circle -> Area: 78.54, Perimeter: 31.42
Rectangle -> Area: 24.00, Perimeter: 20.00

testCases.expectedOutput:
Circle -> Area: 78.54, Perimeter: 31.42
Rectangle -> Area: 24.00, Perimeter: 20.00
Circle -> Area: 314.16, Perimeter: 62.83

Rectangle -> Area: 20.00, Perimeter: 21.00
Circle -> Area: 3.14, Perimeter: 6.28

sourceScreenshot: Bro Code Java Full Course (04:41:19 - Polymorphism)
explanation: Demonstrates abstract base class polymorphism where distinct shapes compute geometrical metrics uniformly.

title: Multi-Vehicle Dynamic Polymorphism Fleet Simulator
description:
Dynamic polymorphism (runtime polymorphism) occurs when the exact method implementation to execute is resolved during program execution based on user selection.

Create a base class `Vehicle` with method `go()` that prints "The vehicle moves".
Create subclasses:
- `Car`: `go()` prints "The car drives forward on the highway"
- `Boat`: `go()` prints "The boat sails across the water"
- `Airplane`: `go()` prints "The airplane flies through the clouds"

The user inputs a numeric choice (1 for Car, 2 for Boat, 3 for Airplane). Instantiate the appropriate subclass into a single `Vehicle` reference variable and call `go()`.

The first line contains an integer N representing the number of vehicle choices.
The second line contains N space-separated integers (1, 2, or 3).
outputFormat: Print the corresponding movement message for each vehicle choice.

The car drives forward on the highway
The boat sails across the water
The airplane flies through the clouds

The boat sails across the water
The airplane flies through the clouds

The car drives forward on the highway
The airplane flies through the clouds

title: Predator and Prey Multi-Interface Simulation
description:
An interface in Java is a template of methods. A class can implement multiple interfaces, allowing developers to model multifaceted behaviors.

Define two interfaces:
- `Prey`: method `void flee()`
- `Predator`: method `void hunt()`

Implement the following creatures:
- `Rabbit`: implements `Prey` -> `flee()` prints "The rabbit is running away!"
- `Hawk`: implements `Predator` -> `hunt()` prints "The hawk is hunting for food!"
- `Fish`: implements BOTH `Prey` AND `Predator` ->
  - `flee()` prints "The fish is fleeing from a larger fish!"
  - `hunt()` prints "The fish is hunting smaller fish!"

Read N creature action queries formatted as '<Creature> <Action>' where Action is 'FLEE' or 'HUNT'. Output the corresponding action or 'Action Not Supported' if the creature does not implement that interface.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of queries.
The next N lines each contain creatureName ('Rabbit', 'Hawk', or 'Fish') and action ('FLEE' or 'HUNT').
outputFormat: Print the triggered action string for each query.
sampleInput:
4
Rabbit FLEE
Hawk HUNT
Fish FLEE
Hawk FLEE
sampleOutput:
The rabbit is running away!
The hawk is hunting for food!
The fish is fleeing from a larger fish!
Action Not Supported

testCases.input:
4
Rabbit FLEE
Hawk HUNT
Fish FLEE
Hawk FLEE
testCases.expectedOutput:
The rabbit is running away!
The hawk is hunting for food!
The fish is fleeing from a larger fish!
Action Not Supported

The fish is hunting smaller fish!
Action Not Supported

testCases.input:
3
Hawk HUNT
Fish FLEE
Fish HUNT
testCases.expectedOutput:
The hawk is hunting for food!
The fish is fleeing from a larger fish!
The fish is hunting smaller fish!

explanation: Illustrates multiple interface implementation where a single entity exhibits multiple contracts.

Interfaces declare standard operations that disparate hardware or software modules must support.

Create a `Playable` interface:
- `void play(String title)`

Implement:
- `AudioPlayer`: `play` prints "Audio Playing: <title>.mp3", `pause` prints "Audio Paused", `stop` prints "Audio Stopped".

- 'VIDEO STOP'

title: Safe Math Division with ArithmeticException & InputMismatchException
description:
An exception is an event that occurs during the execution of a program that disrupts the normal flow of instructions. Handling exceptions prevents programs from crashing.

Write a program that takes two tokens representing a numerator and denominator.
- If the denominator is 0, catch `ArithmeticException` and print: "Error: Cannot divide by zero"
- If either input is not a valid integer, catch `NumberFormatException` and print: "Error: Invalid integer input"
- If inputs are valid and denominator != 0, print the integer division result: "Result: <quotient>".
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of division attempts.
The next N lines each contain two string tokens (numerator and denominator).
outputFormat: Print the result or corresponding error message for each attempt.
constraints: Inputs can be valid integers or non-numeric strings
sampleOutput:
Result: 5
Error: Cannot divide by zero
Error: Invalid integer input

testCases.expectedOutput:
Result: 5
Error: Cannot divide by zero
Error: Invalid integer input

Result: 20
Result: 6

Error: Invalid integer input
Error: Cannot divide by zero
Result: -10

explanation: Illustrates try-catch blocks guarding against runtime arithmetic anomalies and parse failures.

title: Age Verification Registry with Custom InvalidAgeException
description:
Java allows developers to define custom exceptions by extending the `Exception` class. This provides domain-specific error handling.

Create a custom exception `class InvalidAgeException extends Exception`:
- Constructor: `InvalidAgeException(String message) { super(message); }`

Create a method `void checkAge(int age) throws InvalidAgeException`:
- If `age < 18`: throw new InvalidAgeException("Must be at least 18 years old")
- If `age > 120`: throw new InvalidAgeException("Age cannot exceed 120")
- Otherwise: valid.

Given N voter records with name and age, output whether the applicant is registered or print the caught exception message.

The first line contains an integer N representing voter applicants.
The next N lines each contain name (string) and age (int).
outputFormat:
For valid applicants: "Approved: <name> is registered"
For invalid applicants: "Rejected: <name> -> <exceptionMessage>"

title: Inventory Stock Dispenser with InsufficientStockException
description:
Write an inventory dispenser class that tracks available item stock.
Define a custom checked exception `InsufficientStockException`.

A method `void dispense(int requestedQuantity) throws InsufficientStockException`:
- If `requestedQuantity > currentStock`, throw `InsufficientStockException("Requested <requested>, but only <available> remaining")`.

title: Robust Grade Processor with Multi-Catch & Finally Cleanup
description:
The `finally` block in Java always executes regardless of whether an exception was thrown or caught. It is typically used for resource deallocation, logging, and state confirmation.

Given an array of string grade tokens:

- Parse the token at `index` to an integer.
- Catch `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` -> print "Error: Index out of range"
- Catch `NumberFormatException` -> print "Error: Non-numeric grade entry"
- If successful -> print "Grade: <val>"

The second line contains N space-separated tokens.
The third line contains an integer Q representing the number of queries.
The fourth line contains Q space-separated index integers.
outputFormat: For each query, print the result/error followed immediately by the finally message.
constraints: Indices can be negative or >= N

title: Secret Note Logger using FileWriter and FileReader
description:
Bro Code demonstrates writing text with `FileWriter` and streaming characters back using `FileReader.read()`.

In this problem, simulate the file write-read cycle:
1. Read a secret message string from standard input.
2. Write the message into a local file named `secret_note.txt` using `FileWriter`.
3. Open `secret_note.txt` with `FileReader`, read all characters until `.read()` returns -1, and print the retrieved content with its character count.
inputFormat: A single line containing the secret message text.
outputFormat:
Print:
"File Written Successfully"
"Read from File: <content>"
"Characters Read: <length>"
sampleOutput:
File Written Successfully
Read from File: Bro Code Java Masterclass 2026
Characters Read: 30

testCases.expectedOutput:
File Written Successfully
Read from File: Bro Code Java Masterclass 2026
Characters Read: 30

File Written Successfully
Read from File: Hello World
Characters Read: 11

File Written Successfully
Read from File: Keep coding every day!
Characters Read: 22

sourceScreenshot: Bro Code Java Full Course (05:09:15 - FileWriter & 05:12:30 - FileReader)
explanation: Validates file writing and streaming character-by-character reading with proper resource closure.

title: Word and Character Count File Stream Analyzer
description:
Write a text analyzer that computes text file metrics:
Given N lines of text:
1. Count the total number of lines.
2. Count the total number of words (tokens separated by spaces).
3. Count the total number of non-whitespace characters.

Display the summary in a standardized file report format.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the line count.
The next N lines each contain a sentence of text.
outputFormat:
Print:
"Lines: <L> | Words: <W> | Non-Space Chars: <C>"
constraints: Lines contain alphanumeric characters, spaces, and punctuation
sampleInput:
2
Java is powerful and versatile
Practice makes perfect
sampleOutput: Lines: 2 | Words: 8 | Non-Space Chars: 46

testCases.input:
2
Java is powerful and versatile
Practice makes perfect
testCases.expectedOutput: Lines: 2 | Words: 8 | Non-Space Chars: 46
Lines: 1 | Words: 2 | Non-Space Chars: 12

testCases.input:
3
One
Two Three
Four Five Six
testCases.expectedOutput: Lines: 3 | Words: 6 | Non-Space Chars: 22

sourceScreenshot: Bro Code Java Full Course (05:12:30 - File Streams)
explanation: Simulates stream tokenization and character frequency metrics typical of file inspection tools.

title: System Configuration Parser with Key-Value Reader
description:
Configuration files (.properties, .ini) frequently store application settings as `key=value` pairs.

Write a config file parser:
1. Read N configuration lines formatted as `key=value`.
2. Store the pairs in a key-value structure.
3. Read Q query keys and output the resolved setting value or "UNDEFINED" if the key is not present.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing configuration pairs.
The next N lines each contain 'key=value'.
The next line contains an integer Q representing query count.
The next Q lines each contain a query key.
outputFormat: For each query key, print: "<key> = <value>" or "<key> = UNDEFINED".
constraints: Keys and values contain no spaces
sampleOutput:
port = 8080
timeout = UNDEFINED

testCases.expectedOutput:
port = 8080
timeout = UNDEFINED
env = production

ssl = enabled
version = UNDEFINED

sourceScreenshot: Bro Code Java Full Course (05:02:31 - File Handling)
explanation: Simulates reading configuration settings from files into runtime memory mappings.

title: Student Report Card Serializer with Object Streams
description:
Serialization is the process of converting an object's state into a byte stream, allowing it to be persisted to disk or sent over a network. Deserialization reconstructs the object from bytes.

Create a class `StudentRecord implements java.io.Serializable`:
- Fields: `int id`, `String name`, `double gpa`.
- Method: `String getSummary()` -> "ID: <id> | Name: <name> | GPA: <gpa>".

Write a program that:
1. Instantiates a `StudentRecord` from user input.
2. Serializes it into `student.ser` using `ObjectOutputStream`.
3. Deserializes the record back using `ObjectInputStream`.
4. Prints the validated summary.
inputFormat: A single line containing id (int), name (string), and gpa (double).
outputFormat:
Print:
"Serialized Student Successfully"
"Deserialized: ID: <id> | Name: <name> | GPA: <gpa>"
sampleOutput:
Serialized Student Successfully
Deserialized: ID: 101 | Name: Pranav | GPA: 3.95

testCases.expectedOutput:
Serialized Student Successfully
Deserialized: ID: 101 | Name: Pranav | GPA: 3.95

Serialized Student Successfully
Deserialized: ID: 205 | Name: Alice | GPA: 4.00

Serialized Student Successfully
Deserialized: ID: 309 | Name: Bob | GPA: 3.50

sourceScreenshot: Bro Code Java Full Course (Serialization)
explanation: Verifies byte-stream serialization and object resurrection using Java Serializable architecture.

title: CSV Data Table Importer with Formatted Terminal Report
description:
Comma-Separated Values (CSV) is the most ubiquitous tabular data export format.

Write a CSV parser and aggregator:
Given N lines of employee data formatted as: `Name,Department,Salary`
1. Parse each record.
2. Track total payroll expense and find the highest earner.
3. Print each formatted row and a summary footer.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of CSV rows.
The next N lines each contain 'Name,Department,Salary'.
outputFormat:
Print each row as: "[<Department>] <Name> - $<Salary>"
On the next line, print: "Total Payroll: $<sum>"
On the final line, print: "Top Earner: <Name> ($<highestSalary>)"

[Engineering] Alice - $90000
[Marketing] Bob - $65000
[Engineering] Charlie - $110000

title: Java Interactive CLI Calculator Engine
description:
In Bro Code's project portfolio, a console calculator is a cornerstone project demonstrating control flow, switch statements, and arithmetic operators.

Implement an expression calculation engine supporting:
- Addition (`+`)
- Subtraction (`-`)
- Multiplication (`*`)
- Division (`/` with integer division)
- Modulo (`%`)
- Exponentiation (`^` where a^b computes power)

Input commands until 'EXIT' is received. Print each calculation in the format: "<num1> <op> <num2> = <result>".
inputFormat:
Multiple lines each containing 'num1 op num2' (e.g. '12 + 5').
The input ends with 'EXIT'.
outputFormat:
For each calculation, print: "<num1> <op> <num2> = <result>".
If division/modulo by zero occurs, print: "Error: Division by zero".
On termination, print: "Calculator Closed".
sampleOutput:
10 + 5 = 15
20 / 4 = 5
2 ^ 8 = 256
Error: Division by zero
Calculator Closed

testCases.expectedOutput:
10 + 5 = 15
20 / 4 = 5
2 ^ 8 = 256
Error: Division by zero
Calculator Closed

15 * 3 = 45
100 - 45 = 55
Calculator Closed

5 ^ 3 = 125
14 % 4 = 2
Calculator Closed

sourceScreenshot: Bro Code Java Project (Calculator)
explanation: Implements an interactive command-driven arithmetic engine with operator dispatch.

title: Multiple-Choice Trivia Quiz Game Engine
description:
Bro Code's Java Quiz Game features questions arrays, options 2D arrays, player answer validation, and score evaluation.

Build an automated quiz evaluator:
Given 4 questions where the correct answer keys are:
Q1: C (Which keyword creates an object? -> new)
Q2: B (What is the size of int in Java? -> 4 bytes)
Q3: A (Which package contains Scanner? -> java.util)
Q4: D (Which collection allows unique elements only? -> Set)

Read 4 player choices (characters A, B, C, or D). Evaluate each answer, tally the total score out of 4, and display the final performance rating.
inputFormat: A single line containing 4 space-separated characters representing the player's answers (e.g. 'C B A D').
outputFormat:
Print evaluation for each question:
"Q1: Correct!" or "Q1: Incorrect (Correct: C)"
On the next line, print: "Total Score: <score>/4"
On the final line, print performance:
- 4/4: "Grade: Perfect Score!"
- 3/4: "Grade: Great Job!"
- 2/4: "Grade: Good Effort!"
- <= 1/4: "Grade: Keep Practicing!"
constraints: Answers are characters A, B, C, or D

Q1: Correct!
Q2: Correct!
Q3: Correct!
Q4: Correct!
Total Score: 4/4
Grade: Perfect Score!

Grade: Great Job!

title: Tic-Tac-Toe Grid Match Engine
description:
Tic-Tac-Toe is a classic game project taught by Bro Code to master 2D arrays, game state checking, and coordinate translation.

A 3x3 board starts empty (filled with '-'). Players alternate placing 'X' and 'O'.
A player wins if they place 3 of their marks across any row, column, or diagonal.
If all 9 cells are filled and no player has won, it is a Draw.

Read the move sequence (0 to 8 representing cell indices 0..8, where row = idx / 3 and col = idx % 3). Stop immediately when a player wins or all moves are exhausted, and print the outcome.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer M representing the number of moves.
The second line contains M space-separated cell indices (0 to 8). Player 1 is 'X', Player 2 is 'O'.
outputFormat:
Print:
"Winner: Player X" or "Winner: Player O" or "Result: Draw" or "Game Incomplete"
constraints: All moves in input are unique
sampleOutput: Winner: Player X

testCases.expectedOutput: Winner: Player X
Result: Draw
Winner: Player O

sourceScreenshot: Bro Code Java Project (Tic Tac Toe)
explanation: Encapsulates 2D board state manipulation, alternate turn dispatch, and victory condition evaluation.

An extended version of the Rock-Paper-Scissors game project taught by Bro Code.
Rules:

- Paper covers Rock
- Rock crushes Lizard

The next N lines each contain Player 1 move and Player 2 move (Rock, Paper, Scissors, Lizard, Spock).
outputFormat:
Print each round: "Round <i>: <Winner>" (where Winner is 'Player 1', 'Player 2', or 'Tie').
On the final line, print the champion: "Champion: Player 1" or "Champion: Player 2" or "Tournament Tie".

title: Audio Playlist & Track Duration Manager
description:
Bro Code's course features an Audio Player project utilizing Clip and AudioInputStream.

Model a music playlist management system:
Each track has a `title` (String), `artist` (String), and `durationSeconds` (int).
Given N tracks:
1. List each track formatted as: "[Track <i>] <title> by <artist> (<mm:ss>)"
2. Compute the total playlist run time and format it as `HH:MM:SS` (or `MM:SS` if under 1 hour).
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the track count.
The next N lines each contain title, artist, and durationSeconds.
outputFormat:
Print each track on a separate line.
On the final line, print: "Total Duration: <formattedTime>".
constraints: Titles and artists have no spaces

title: Console Text Editor & Note-Keeper
description:
Bro Code's Text Editor project introduces file saving, text manipulation, and line indexing.

Implement a console-based notepad:
Supports commands:
- `APPEND <text>`: adds a line to the end of the document.
- `DELETE <lineIndex>`: deletes the 1-based line index (or prints "Error: Line not found").
- `SEARCH <keyword>`: prints 1-based line numbers containing keyword, or "Not found".
- `SAVE`: prints the complete document lines and exits.
inputFormat: A series of command lines ending with 'SAVE'.
outputFormat: Print action confirmations and the final saved document.
sampleInput:
APPEND First line of code
APPEND Second line of notes
SEARCH notes
DELETE 1
SAVE
sampleOutput:
Matches: Line 2
Deleted: Line 1
--- Document Content ---
Second line of notes
--- End of File ---

testCases.input:
APPEND First line of code
APPEND Second line of notes
SEARCH notes
DELETE 1
SAVE
testCases.expectedOutput:
Matches: Line 2
Deleted: Line 1
--- Document Content ---
Second line of notes
--- End of File ---

testCases.input:
APPEND Hello World
SEARCH Java
SAVE
testCases.expectedOutput:
Matches: None
--- Document Content ---
Hello World
--- End of File ---

testCases.input:
APPEND Item A
APPEND Item B
DELETE 5
SAVE
testCases.expectedOutput:
Error: Line not found
--- Document Content ---
Item A
Item B
--- End of File ---

explanation: Manages in-memory document line state with index-safe insertion and deletion operations.

title: Bank ATM Transaction Terminal Simulator
description:
An interactive banking ATM machine simulator:
- Account has a PIN (e.g. 1234) and initial balance B.
- If PIN does not match, reject access: "Access Denied: Incorrect PIN" and exit.
- If PIN matches:
  - `DEPOSIT <amount>`: balance += amount. Print: "Deposited $<amt> | Balance: $<bal>"
  - `WITHDRAW <amount>`: if balance >= amount, balance -= amount. Print: "Withdrew $<amt> | Balance: $<bal>". Otherwise: "Insufficient Funds"
  - `STATEMENT`: print current balance.
inputFormat:
The first line contains correctPIN (string) and enteredPIN (string).
The second line contains initialBalance (int).
The next lines contain commands ending with 'EXIT'.
outputFormat: Print transaction logs and current balance.
constraints: Balances and amounts are positive integers
sampleOutput:
Deposited $200 | Balance: $700
Withdrew $100 | Balance: $600
Insufficient Funds
ATM Session Closed

testCases.expectedOutput:
Deposited $200 | Balance: $700
Withdrew $100 | Balance: $600
Insufficient Funds
ATM Session Closed
Access Denied: Incorrect PIN

Deposited $50 | Balance: $150
ATM Session Closed

sourceScreenshot: Bro Code Java Project (ATM Machine)
explanation: Implements an authenticated finite-state interactive banking transaction engine.

title: Dice Roller & Statistical Probability Engine
description:
Bro Code's Random Numbers and Game Logic modules demonstrate dice simulation and statistical distribution.

When rolling two standard 6-sided dice, the possible sums range from 2 to 12.
Given the outcomes of N rolls of two dice (each roll provided as two integers between 1 and 6):
1. Compute the sum for each roll.
2. Tally the frequency of each sum (2 through 12).
3. Identify the most frequent sum (if tied, print the lower sum).
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of rolls.
The next N lines each contain two integers d1 and d2 (1 <= d1, d2 <= 6).
outputFormat:
Print each occurring sum and its count: "Sum <val>: <count> times" (in ascending order of sum).
On the final line, print: "Most Frequent Sum: <val>".
sampleOutput:
Sum 2: 1 times
Sum 7: 3 times
Sum 8: 1 times
Most Frequent Sum: 7

testCases.expectedOutput:
Sum 2: 1 times
Sum 7: 3 times
Sum 8: 1 times
Most Frequent Sum: 7

Sum 12: 2 times
Most Frequent Sum: 12

Sum 5: 3 times
Most Frequent Sum: 5

sourceScreenshot: Bro Code Java Project (Dice Roller)
explanation: Tabulates composite sum occurrences across simulated random experiment events.

title: Snake Board Grid Navigation Simulator
description:
Bro Code's Java Snake Game tutorial is an iconic project featuring 2D coordinate movement, collision detection, and tail growth.

Simulate a snake navigation engine on an N x N grid (0-indexed from (0,0) at top-left to (N-1, N-1)):
- Snake starts at (0, 0) with initial length 1.
- Move commands: 'U' (row - 1), 'D' (row + 1), 'L' (col - 1), 'R' (col + 1).
- Food is located at given coordinates (foodR, foodC). When the head reaches the food, the snake eats it: length increments by 1, and food is consumed.
- If the snake attempts to move outside the grid boundaries [0, N-1], the move causes a collision: print "Collision at (<r>, <c>)! Game Over" and stop immediately.
- If all moves are executed without collision, print: "Success: Final Position (<r>, <c>) | Length: <len>".
inputFormat:
The first line contains grid size N.
The second line contains food coordinates foodR and foodC.
The third line contains move string (e.g. 'RRDLL').
outputFormat: Print the game outcome and final statistics.
constraints: Moves are letters U, D, L, R
sampleOutput: Success: Final Position (2, 1) | Length: 2

testCases.expectedOutput: Success: Final Position (2, 1) | Length: 2
Collision at (0, 3)! Game Over
Success: Final Position (0, 2) | Length: 2

sourceScreenshot: Bro Code Java Project (Snake Game)
explanation: Simulates 2D state machine transitions, boundary clipping, and goal ingestion logic.
